name: Buffalo Valley Designated Camping Area
note: Bridger-Teton NF designated undeveloped sites strung along the paved Buffalo Valley Road from US 26/287 east of Moran to Turpin Meadow; camping only at the marked, numbered sites. A few open straight off the paved road (site 1 is a large gravel pullout above the Buffalo Fork); most lie down short dirt spurs the Forest Service rates for high-clearance vehicles, and in 2024 a camper found one spur blocked partway in. Call the Blackrock Ranger District about conditions before setting out. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: Bridger-Teton NF camping page (read 2026-11-20), Jackson and Blackrock Ranger District Designated Undeveloped Sites table: 'Buffalo Valley - No. First come, first served. - From Jackson, take Hwy 26/89 north to Moran then turn east towards Dubois. Turn left at sign for Turpin Meadow Recreation area. - Scenic valley along wild and scenic river with mix of ranches and forest area. Road is narrow but paved.'; FS designated-sites brochure (Camping at Designated Sites trifold, FS-authored 2025-03, hosted on visitjacksonhole.com) lists Buffalo Valley, 23 sites, '14 day stay limit year-round', with a numbered site map; USFS EDW road layer: the access road (Buffalo Valley Road) is not an FS road (county, paved per the FS), the site spurs 30085/30086/30069/30069A/30050B/30050E/30071/30071A are maintenance level 2 'HIGH CLEARANCE VEHICLES'; Esri imagery shows site 1 (the pin) as a gravel pullout directly beside the paved road with a camper/trailer parked, and site 9 as a gravel loop at the mouth of FR 30069 by the paved road; The Dyrt (12 reviews, 4.8): an RV (2022), truck camper (2023), E350 camper van (2026), site 1 'a large roadside pullout' -> agency-designated drive-in sites, some reached without any level-2 road (small free NF sites rule, call-first caveat). Not on recreation.gov.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World_Imagery (rendered) at z17 (~1 km frame) and z18 (~330 m frame) on 43.8441,-110.4048, USFS MVUM roads drawn on: site 1, the gravel pullout on paved Buffalo Valley Road, sits ~100 m N of the Buffalo Fork (here ~40 m of open water with gravel bars, a river) across an open sage meadow, a little above it; FR 30085 runs E from the pullout to a clearing ~70 m from the bank (a vehicle parked). The Dyrt: site 1 'elevated views', overlooks the river from above, 2025 reviewer found no path down to the river. Sites 2-3 are reported 'closer to the creek' but no pad could be placed within ~50 m of the water from the imagery or the FS site map -> defaults down to riverview (open view across the meadow), not riverfront. Sites 9-23 sit along the road and spurs back from the river.
fees_source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/recreation/camping-cabins ('Dispersed camping (outside campgrounds) is free in the remote areas of the Forest'; the Buffalo Valley row lists no fee, 'No. First come, first served.'), read 2026-11-20

booking.note: Camping only at the marked, designated sites; 14-day limit year-round (Buffalo Valley is in the Blackrock Ranger District, outside the Jackson RD 5-day summer order).

flags: ROAD LAYER (as asked): USFS EDW_RoadBasic_01 / EDW_MVUM_02 (queried 2026-11-20). The main access, Buffalo Valley Road, is not in the FS layer at all (county road; the FS calls it 'narrow but paved'). The spurs the sites sit on, placed from the FS brochure's numbered site map against the layer: sites 1-3 on FR 30085 'BUFFALO VALLEY DISPERSED CAMP' (0.2 mi), 4-8 on FR 30086 'BUFFALO VALLEY ROAD DISPERSED' (0.25 mi), 9-13 on FR 30069 'BUFFALO RIVER' / 30069A 'BURRO HILL ROAD' / 30069C, 14 on FR 30050B 'BUFFALO FORK ACCESS', 15-23 near FR 30050E 'OUTFITTER SPUR' and 30071/30071A 'BUFFALO RIVER SPUR'/'DISPERSED CAMP SPUR' - all maintenance level '2 - HIGH CLEARANCE VEHICLES', native surface (MVUM open to motorhomes 05/01-11/30). Not every site needs level-2 travel: site 1 is a gravel pullout touching the paved road at the mouth of 30085 (imagery: camper/trailer parked there), and site 9 is a gravel loop ~50 m off the paved road at the mouth of 30069. The pin is site 1. Site 14A sits beside FR 30050D (ML3) but that spur leads to private ranch buildings, so I did not count it. If the reviewer reads the ML2 rule per spur rather than per site, this becomes a skip ('high clearance'); the FS text does not name RVs for Buffalo Valley (it does for Spread Creek).

ACCESS WORDING: the FS says only 'Road is narrow but paved' - no RV, trailer, 4WD or high-clearance statement and no rig limit. Campers (The Dyrt): a Honda Civic managed the road to site 3 (2023), 'high clearance is easier' (2023), 'road was blocked about half a mile in, leaving roughly 3 sites accessible' (2024-07, a spur). Campendium (refuses, 403) was not opened; a search snippet credits its site-9 page with '30 ft max RV length' and room for 'at least 4 rigs' - not used as evidence.
PHONE: FS camping and Buffalo Valley Area pages give the Blackrock Ranger District as 307-543-3900; the 2025 brochure prints (307) 543-2386. Wrote the FS page's number.
SITE POSITIONS are approximate: georeferenced from the brochure's small inset (control points Hatchet and Turpin Meadow campgrounds), then checked on imagery for sites 1-3 and 9 only.
WATERFRONT: sites 2-3 may be riverfront (reviews: 'lower and closer to the creek', a river 'right next to the site'), but no pad was placed within ~50 m from imagery; left at riverview.
SEASON not written: the brochure's year-round 14-day limit and the spurs' MVUM dates (05/01-11/30) are not a campground season.

POSSIBLE NEW LEAD (not vetted): the FS camping page lists 'Blackrock Meadows' under 'RV and Camper Van Areas - Great for large RVs' ('Drive 15 miles [east of Moran]. The RV park will be on the left. Large, flat area for RVs and vans ... No campfires.', 50+ sites in the brochure); no DB entry by that name and nothing in the DB between Hatchet (6473) and Togwotee. Moran Vista (the other RV area) is 6493.
